codes.title: Pneumonia, organism unspecified
codes.rationale: The patient presents with fever, productive cough, and focal crackles with bronchial breathing, which are consistent with community-acquired pneumonia. However, the lack of imaging means the assignment is provisional.

evidence.quote: 4 days of fever and cough, now bringing up thick green sputum, sharp right-sided pain on deep breath. Temp 38.6, RR 24, sats 95% on air, pulse 104, BP 112/70. Coarse crackles at the right base with bronchial breathing there.
Fever, productive cough and focal crackles with dullness to percussion over the affected zone are sufficient to assign community-acquired pneumonia in the primary care setting.

Effective with this revision, a definitive pneumonia assignment rests on radiographic or point-of-care ultrasound confirmation of consolidation recorded in the encounter. Auscultatory findings together with fever and purulent sputum support a provisional assignment carrying moderate confidence, and the provisional status is retained in the record until imaging is available.

would_lower_confidence: Absence of fever, productive cough, or focal crackles, or presence of an alternative explanation for the symptoms.

codes.title: Severe pre-eclampsia
codes.rationale: The patient is a 29-year-old female, 30+2 weeks pregnant, presenting with headache, visual disturbances, and significant hypertension (BP 168/112 and 165/110) with proteinuria (urine dipstick protein 3+). These findings meet the criteria for severe pre-eclampsia as per GDL-028.

evidence.quote: 29F, G2P1, 30+2 weeks by dating scan. Two days of headache across the forehead and flashing lights in vision this morning. Swelling of hands and face noticed by her husband. BP 168/112, repeated after 15 minutes 165/110. Urine dipstick protein 3+.

New hypertension arising after twenty weeks of gestation with proteinuria, or with any of headache, visual disturbance, right upper quadrant or epigastric pain, hyperreflexia or a falling platelet count, is pre-eclampsia. The same hypertension after twenty weeks without proteinuria and without those features is gestational hypertension. Hypertension recorded before twenty weeks belongs to the chronic hypertension group carried into pregnancy. Severity features moving the assignment to the severe entry are systolic pressure at or above 160, platelets below 100, deranged transaminases, or pulmonary oedema.

confidence_rationale: The documented findings of headache, visual disturbances, significant hypertension, and proteinuria in a pregnant woman at 30+2 weeks meet the criteria for severe pre-eclampsia as per GDL-028. No other condition in the catalogue accounts for these findings equally well.
would_raise_confidence: Further documentation of deranged transaminases or pulmonary oedema would confirm the severity of pre-eclampsia.
would_lower_confidence: Documentation of normal blood pressure or absence of proteinuria would lower the confidence in the assignment.
